subject: Invoice discrepancy and overage reconciliation for Jan usage
messages:
From: Kimberly Cho <kim.cho@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Oliver Moss <oliver.moss@acmehealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected overage on January invoice

Hi Ben —

We just received the January invoice (attached) and noticed a $3,980 overage compared to our expected monthly spend. Our engineers pulled the attached usage_export-202601.csv and the token totals in the invoice don't match the CSV at a glance. Can you help reconcile:

- Which models and routes contributed to the overage line?
- Is there any chance of double-counting (we had a deployment change on 2026-01-10)?
- How will VAT be handled on any credit/adjustment?

We need a short explanation and a proposed remediation so we can close this on our side — procurement is waiting to release payment pending clarification.

Appreciate a quick response.

Thanks,
Kimberly Cho
Head of Procurement
Acme Health Inc.
Attachments: invoice-202601.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Cho <kim.cho@acmehealth.com>, Oliver Moss <oliver.moss@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on January invoice

Hi Kimberly — thanks for flagging this and attaching the CSV. I’m copying Laura (Sales Ops) and Rishi (Finance) to run a reconciliation; well look at model-level usage and the 2026-01-10 deployment window you mentioned.

Immediate next steps:
- Ill ask Sales Ops to cross-check our billing meter against the export for 2026-01-01 -> 2026-01-15.
- Finance will prepare a provisional credit if we find miscounting.
- I can set up a 30-minute call tomorrow if youd like to walk through the numbers together.

Kimberly — is 11:00 AM PT tomorrow a good time for a quick call?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0191

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Kimberly Cho <kim.cho@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Jan 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Reconciliation notes for Acme overage (Jan)

Ben / Rishi —

I pulled the meter logs and matched them against the CSV Kimberly provided (usage_export-202601.csv). Summary of findings:

- Root cause: On 2026-01-10 a rolling deployment to a legacy proxy caused duplicated request headers for a subset of requests to the /chat/completions route. Our meter dedup logic used a header that was duplicated by the proxy, so ~1,220,000 tokens were billed twice between 01/10 and 01/12.

- Impact: The duplicated tokens translate to an overage of $2,450 (USD) on Acme's January invoice. I attached a small reconciliation worksheet (we included per-day token deltas).

- VAT: the overage is taxable in the US jurisdiction as part of the invoice. If we apply a credit note, Finance will issue a credit for $2,450; the credit will carry VAT reversal information that Acme can use for local filings. Rishi: can you confirm the exact VAT reversal language we put on the credit note?

Proposed remediation:
1) Issue a credit note for $2,450 applied to the Jan invoice.
2) Send Acme an updated invoice/statement reflecting the credit and VAT reversal details.
3) Apply a short-term guardrail: well run additional dedup checks for the next billing cycle and proactively notify if any unexpected spikes are detected.

Ive attached the token reconciliation extract (usage_export-202601.csv) and a one-page summary for Kimberly.

Laura Bennett
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
Attachments: usage_export-202601.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Cho <kim.cho@acmehealth.com>, Oliver Moss <oliver.moss@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 Jan 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on January invoice — proposed credit applied

Hi Kimberly / Oliver —

Thanks for your patience while we investigated. Short summary and next steps:

- Root cause: internal proxy duplication during the 2026-01-10 deployment caused ~1,220,000 tokens to be double-counted (confirmed by Sales Ops).
- Amount: We will issue a credit of $2,450 USD to offset the overage on your January invoice.
- VAT: The credit will include a VAT reversal entry. This will not change your VAT registration — it simply documents the reversal for your records. If you need a formal VAT credit memo, Rishi will attach the standardized wording.
- Timing: The credit will be applied to your account today; you should see the updated invoice/statement within 3 business days and the credit reflected on the next billing statement (or as a payment offset if the invoice has already been paid).

I attached the updated statement and a short reconciliation extract. Please let me know if you need anything else — we can also schedule a quick call if you want to review the line-by-line tokens.

If youd like us to permanently increase the monitoring threshold on your tenant to alert on similar anomalies, we can enable that as well (no charge).

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0191

Attachments: credit-note-ACME-202601.pdf, updated-statement-ACME-202601.pdf
